tool_input.command: ls; ls gpufe methods roles 2>&1 | head -50; for f in work/findings/F-*.json; do echo "== $f"; head -c 900 $f; echo; done
tool_input.description: List code dirs and skim findings

result:
I've written the round 2 safety verdict to `work/board/r0002/safety.json` (it parses as valid JSON). My working notes are in `work/agents/safety/r0002_notes.md` and `s02_insertion_numbers.py`.

**Unchecked numbers:** I still can't run Python in this role, so I worked the S2 figures by hand. I did check them against the analyst's 35–41 % compression figure and they match. Someone with permission should run the script to confirm them (change request CR-EXEC).

**Main findings**
- **S2 (insertion), critical:** the current rule can't be computed by a program. Its "hard PLCL strain ≤ 3 %" limit goes past the material's elastic limit in 3 of the 9 material assumptions (as low as 1.7 %), so the part would be permanently deformed. My proposed replacement:
  - Temporary distraction during surgery: at most 2.0 mm parallel.
  - Insertion paths tried: straight in, or angled ±15° or ±30°.
  - The hard core must fit through the gap with no compression at all, which caps it at 2.95 + 2.0 = 4.95 mm tall.
  - Soft parts may be compressed by at most 30 % (the current 40 % has no evidence behind it).
  - The worst insertion position gets a stress check: at most half the low-strength value.
- **What that does to the designs:** the tallest middle-to-back region ends up mostly soft or empty. A shape that fits in from the front also has little shape left to stop it sliding backward (about 0.35 mm of overlap on the midline). So the cord-side criteria should be checked at a friction coefficient of 0.2, not 0.3 (CR-S9b).
- **The 135 N push-out floor will probably be very hard to meet:** with friction alone it needs a clamp force of 225–338 N. Earlier simulations only reached 18–115 N. The PI should know this rather than see the floor lowered quietly.
- **Temporary distraction limit:** I found no published limit in millimetres for distraction during surgery. The 2 mm default comes from Hsueh 2023 (Sci Rep), which is about the final disc-height gain: a gain of 2 mm or more raised subsidence from 31 % to 47 % and adjacent-segment changes from 15 % to 48 %. A 2013 J Korean Neurosurg Soc study found more postoperative neck pain when the distraction torque was above 6 kgf·cm. A surgeon still needs to confirm the value.
- **Friction:** no measured friction coefficient exists for PEEK, PLA or PLCL on vertebral bone. A Europe PMC search returned 40 hits, all simulation studies that assume a value. Smooth metal on bone measures 0.16–0.41. I recommend a small coupon friction test.
- **New missing safety items:**
  - Pushing the cage too deep toward the cord during insertion: nothing checks this, so I propose an inserter with a depth stop (critical).
  - Fatigue at contact hot spots: the lab's earlier PLA cages all cracked at the same two places at the back.
  - Soft PLCL tearing or peeling off the hard core as it slides in, leaving debris.
  - Nothing yet checks the cage after 16 weeks, when the material is weaker and the clamp force has relaxed.
- **Still open from round 1:** `constraints.py` doesn't exist, so the designer must not start yet. There is no `work/requests/` folder, so no change request is being tracked. S8 (bone overload) still has no number.

Every constraint has a plain Traditional Chinese explanation with an everyday comparison, and `summary_zh` gives the PI the overview. All values remain recommendations until the PI approves them.
